title: Hasten, O Sinner, to Be Wise
description: Hasten, O Sinner, to Be Wise in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Scott wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 55.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Has-ten, O sin-ner, to be wise And stay not for the mor-row’s sun, The lon-ger wis-dom you de-spise, The hard-er is she to be won.

lines: Hasten, O sinner, to be wise
And stay not for the morrow’s sun,
The harder is she to be won.
And stay not for the morrow’s sun,
For fear thy season should be o’er
Before this evening’s course be run.
And stay not for the morrow’s sun,
For fear thy lamp should fail to burn
Before the needful work is done.
Hasten, O sinner, to be blest
And stay not for the morrow’s sun,
For fear the curse should thee arrest

licence: Public domain: Thomas Scott died in 1775.
credits: Words by Thomas Scott (1705–1775), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
